slides.title: OpenAI Strawberry Model Preview This morning I have
slides.text: OpenAI Strawberry Model Preview This morning I have tested o1-preview and o1-mini. One of the tests was to analyze a 87KB JSON file containing 76 news items (title, text, tags, dates, etc.. ) - and return the list of titles in the order of importance. I was really impressed by o1-preview model. o1-mini was not as good and can not be trusted. How OpenAI made o1 "think" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNE6QZaRavo Reinforcement learning, generating helper tokens, chain-of-thought processing, "think" before responding Matthew Berman: GPT-o1: The Best Model I've Ever Tested https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SbrfjBV8EzM o1 model is designed for handling complex, multistep problems with improved reasoning skills. good for coding, math, science. outperforms expert humans on PhD-level science questions ranks in the 89th percentile for competitive programming. solved 83% of International Mathematics Olympiad qualifying exam problems, compared to GPT-4o's 13%. security test score: 84% vs 22% of previous generation. Cost $15 / $60  in/out per Million tokens

slides.title: Reflection-70B Matt Shumer https://x.com/mattshumer_ https://www.hyperwriteai.com Sahil Chaudhary https://twitter.com/csahil28
slides.text: Reflection-70B Matt Shumer https://x.com/mattshumer_ https://www.hyperwriteai.com Sahil Chaudhary https://twitter.com/csahil28 https://glaive.ai Matt Berman videos: 35 min interview with Matt & Sahil https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5_m-kN64Exc How This AI Model Achieves Insane Accuracy https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-IBAg6lMfXA Matt Shumer & Sahil Chaudhary have fine-tuned Llama 3.1 70B  and claimed (September 5th) to achieve amazing accuracy beating top models in just 3 weeks. They used a technique similar to the one described in 2023 paper " Reflection-Tuning: Recycling Data for Better Instruction-Tuning "  - basically training the model to use "step-by-step" Chain of Thought approach. This is done by tuning on synthetic data showing examples of using <thinking> and <reflection> tags to remove hallucination and perform self-correction - and fine-tuned the model on these examples. https://openreview.net/forum?id=xaqoZZqkPU https://venturebeat.com/ai/meet-the-new-most-powerful-open-source-ai-model-in-the-world-hyperwrites-reflection-70b/ https://huggingface.co/mattshumer/Reflection-Llama-3.1-70B But third party evaluations have failed to reproduce Reflection 70B’s impressive results, so Shumer was accused of fraud. https://www.greenbot.com/hyperwrite-reflection-70B/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Alzjn_0ne1Y https://venturebeat.com/ai/reflection-70b-model-maker-breaks-silence-amid-fraud-accusations/

slides.title: Chai Discovery Chai Discovery , an AI biology
slides.text: Chai Discovery Chai Discovery , an AI biology startup founded six months ago Raised nearly $30 million from Thrive Capital and OpenAI Released Chai-1 - a new multi-modal foundation model for molecular structure prediction Chai-1 enables unified prediction of proteins, small molecules, DNA, RNA, covalent modifications, and more. The model is available for free via a web interface, including for commercial applications such as drug discovery. slides.title: Misc 4 Jim Fan - fooling LLM benchmarks
slides.text: Misc 4 Jim Fan - fooling LLM benchmarks https://x.com/DrJimFan/status/1833160432833716715 Train on paraphrased examples of the test set. LLM-decontaminator" paper from LMSys found that you can beat GPT-4 with a 13B model (!!) It's easy to game the LLM-decontaminator as well. It only checks for paraphrasing, but you can use any frontier model to generate "new questions" with similar logic You can also prompt-engineer the heck out of your generator to fool the LLM-decontaminator Increasing inference-time almost always helps. Self-reflection (see Reflexion, Shinn et al. 2023), simple majority voting or Tree of Thought. These are essentially ensemble methods. Ensemble of N things > 1 thing if you don't control for inference-time tokens. Model Collapse - AI models, trained on their own generated synthetic data, gradually produce lower-quality outputs. This cycle worsens with each iteration of retraining, leading to what is called "model collapse" . Anthropic Claude Artifacts to build: Code snippets: Can be in any coding language. Webpages: Single page HTML, CSS, and Javascript. Mermaid diagrams: Flow charts and other diagrams. Documents: Markdown formatted docs. SVG images: Simple vector drawings. React components: Interactive apps. RefChecker - standardized assessment to identify hallucinations https://github.com/amazon-science/RefChecker https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w-fl1xR9dj0 Alexis Conneau - one of OpenAI‘s research leads for its ChatGPT-4o audio product, is leaving to launch a startup DocAI - extract structured info from documents: https://github.com/madisonmay/docai iText2KG - Python package uses LLM to extract entities and relationships from text, incrementally building consistent knowledge graphs - https://github.com/AuvaLab/itext2kg

slides.title: Google Data Gemma RAG & RIG 27B models
slides.text: Google Data Gemma RAG & RIG 27B models Improving accuracy of LLMs by integrating them with Data Commons - a vast, open-source repository of public statistics from trusted organizations like the United Nations (UN), Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and global census bureaus. RIG (Retrieval Interleaved Generation) - LLM is trained to produce natural language queries to retrieve data from Data Commons RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) - relevant data tables are fetched from Data Commons and used to augment the LLM's prompt https://www.threads.net/@qnixsynapse/post/C_0Z3I9yYRD https://huggingface.co/google/datagemma-rag-27b-it https://huggingface.co/google/datagemma-rig-27b-it https://docs.datacommons.org/papers/DataGemma-FullPaper.pdf https://research.google/blog/grounding-ai-in-reality-with-a-little-help-from-data-commons/
